questions.explain: A SOAP mock doesn't return its answer; it drops it in a map. `doInvoke` is `void` and puts the response element under `'response_x'`. The class can be `public` and `@IsTest`, which keeps it out of the 6 MB code size limit.
wrong: `doInvoke` is `void`; the reply goes into the response map.
SOAP mocks are registered with `WebServiceMock.class`.
`WebServiceMock` alone covers WSDL2Apex callouts.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Test Web Service Callouts

questions.q: A Queueable that implements `Database.AllowsCallouts` sends invoices to an ERP system. Its test fails with an error saying test methods don't support callouts. What is the fix?
options: Move the insert after `Test.startTest()`, so uncommitted work doesn't block the callout when the job runs
Add `Database.AllowsCallouts` to the test class as well, so its test methods are allowed to make callouts
Call `Test.setMock` inside the Queueable's `execute()` method
Call `Test.setMock` before `Test.stopTest()`, ideally before enqueuing, because the job runs at `stopTest`
questions.explain: The mock must be in place before the job runs. The queued job runs at `Test.stopTest()`, so register the mock before then, ideally before enqueuing.
wrong: DML before `startTest` is the recommended order and isn't the cause here.
`AllowsCallouts` marks async classes, not test classes.
Test setup doesn't belong in production code; the test registers the mock.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Queueable Apex; Testing HTTP Callouts by Implementing the HttpCalloutMock Interface

questions.q: An architect plans to replace slow dependencies with `Test.createStub()` across a service layer. Which two of these classes can NOT be stubbed with the Stub API? (Choose 2)
options: `AccountCleanupBatch`, which implements `Database.Batchable<SObject>`
`PricingService`, a `public` top-level class with a `public` no-argument constructor
`TaxCalculator`, a `public virtual` class whose methods return `Map<String, Object>`
`RegistryService`, a top-level class whose only constructor is `private`
`ShippingClient`, a `public` top-level class in the same namespace as the test
questions.explain: The Stub API needs a class it can build and extend from outside. It can't mock Batchable classes or classes with only private constructors. It also can't mock static or private methods, properties, triggers, inner classes or system types.
wrong: A public top-level class with an accessible constructor can be stubbed.
Map return types are fine; only iterators can't be used as return or parameter types.
A class in the same namespace as the `createStub` call can be stubbed.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Build a Mocking Framework with the Stub API

questions.q: `CatalogService` has two overloads, `Decimal getPrice(String)` and `Decimal getPrice(String, Integer)`, plus `Boolean isActive(String)`. Given the stub provider and test code below, what are `a`, `b` and `c`?
options: `a = null, b = 30, c = null`
questions.explain: Every call on the stub goes to `handleMethodCall`, which checks its branches in order. The two-argument overload hits the first branch (10 × 3 = 30). The one-argument call falls to the Decimal branch (1.5), and `isActive` gets null.
wrong: The real methods never run, and nothing in the provider returns true.
The two-argument call hits the first branch, and null isn't turned into false.
The one-argument call matches the Decimal return-type branch.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Build a Mocking Framework with the Stub API

questions.q: An ISV team writes its tests in its own namespace, acme. They want `Test.createStub()` to stub a service class from a partner's managed package (namespace ptnr), and they keep their `StubProvider` in a shared utility package with a third namespace. What is true?
options: It works, as long as the partner's class is `global` and `virtual`
It fails: the stubbed class must be in the test's namespace; the `StubProvider` can be in any namespace
It fails: the `StubProvider` must be in the same namespace as the stubbed class; the test can be anywhere
It works only if the test is annotated `@IsTest(SeeAllData=true)`
questions.explain: The stubbed class must live in the same namespace as the `Test.createStub()` call. The `StubProvider` can live in any namespace. So stubbing the partner's class from acme fails.
wrong: Being `global` doesn't lift the namespace rule.
It's the other way around: the stubbed class must match the test, and the provider can be anywhere.
Data access has nothing to do with stubbing.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Build a Mocking Framework with the Stub API

questions.q: A `productCard` component uses `@wire(getRecord)`. The Jest test below fails because the `.name` element is empty. What is the most likely fix?
options: Append the element to the DOM before calling `getRecord.emit()`; wire data only reaches a connected component
Replace `await Promise.resolve()` with `jest.runAllTimers()`
Register the adapter with `registerLdsTestWireAdapter(getRecord)` before emitting, so `emit()` reaches the component
Query `document.querySelector('.name')` instead of using the `shadowRoot`
questions.explain: A component only gets wire data once it's on the page. Emitting before `appendChild` sends the data to no one. Append first, then emit, then await a promise before checking.
wrong: The re-render is a microtask, not a timer, so awaiting a resolved promise is right.
Current `sfdx-lwc-jest` doesn't need registration, and the element must still be connected first.
Elements inside the component are reachable only through `element.shadowRoot`.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Write Jest Tests for Lightning Web Components That Use the Wire Service

questions.q: In `contactTile`, clicking the link runs `this.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('select', { detail: this.contact.Id }))`. The test below fails because the handler is never called. What should change?
options: Make the test `async` and `await Promise.resolve()` before clicking
Dispatch the event with `bubbles: true` and `composed: true` so the test can receive it
Use `dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click'))` instead of `click()`
Listen for `'select'`, not `'onselect'`. The `on` prefix is only used for handlers in a parent's template
questions.explain: A listener must use the event's exact name. The event was dispatched as `'select'`, so listen for `'select'`. The `onselect` form is only for handlers in a parent's HTML.
wrong: The listener name never matches, so waiting doesn't help.
The test listens on the host element, which gets the event without bubbling.
`click()` already fires a click event on the link.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Create and Dispatch Events; Test Lightning Web Components

questions.q: A Jest test for a refresh button throws `TypeError`: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'click'). The component template contains `<lightning-button label="Refresh" onclick={handleRefresh}>`. What is wrong?
options: Base components like `lightning-button` aren't rendered in Jest, so the test must click a native button instead
The button is in the component's shadow tree, so find it with `element.shadowRoot.querySelector()`
The test must await a promise before `appendChild()` so the template renders
`document.querySelector` only works after `jest.useFakeTimers()` is called
questions.explain: What a component renders lives inside its shadow tree. Page-level queries like `document.querySelector` can't see in there. Use `element.shadowRoot.querySelector()`.
wrong: `sfdx-lwc-jest` supplies stubs for base components, so `lightning-button` is there to click.
The first render happens on `appendChild`; nothing needs awaiting before it.
Timers have nothing to do with DOM queries.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: DOM Inspection Tests Are Subject to Change; Test Lightning Web Components

questions.q: A component uses `@wire(getContactList)`, imported from `'@salesforce/apex/ContactController.getContactList'`. The test below throws `TypeError`: `getContactList.emit` is not a function. What should the `jest.mock` factory return?
options: `{ default: jest.fn().mockResolvedValue(mockContacts) }`
Keep the factory as it is and call `getContactList.mockResolvedValue(mockContacts)` in the test instead of `emit()`
`{ default: createApexTestWireAdapter(jest.fn()) }`, with the helper required from `'@salesforce/sfdx-lwc-jest'`
`{ emit: jest.fn() }`, so the test can spy on `emit`
questions.explain: Wired Apex needs a wire adapter mock, not a plain function. Make the default export `createApexTestWireAdapter(jest.fn())`, which gives you `emit()` and `error()`. A plain `jest.fn()` only suits imperative calls.
wrong: A resolved promise is for imperative calls, and this mock still has no `emit()`.
The component never calls a wired method as a promise, so the value never arrives.
The component imports the default export, so that export must be the wire adapter.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Write Jest Tests for Lightning Web Components That Use the Wire Service (lwc-recipes apexWireMethodToProperty test)

questions.q: A developer must prove that `accountHeader` passes its `recordId` and the right fields to `getRecord`, without checking the DOM. `NAME_FIELD` is imported from `@salesforce/schema` in both files. Which assertion does this?
options: `expect(getRecord.getLastConfig()).toEqual({ recordId: '001xx000003DGb2AAG', fields: [NAME_FIELD] })`
`expect(getRecord).toHaveBeenCalledWith('001xx000003DGb2AAG')`
`expect(element.account.data.id).toBe('001xx000003DGb2AAG')`
`expect(getRecord.emit).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ recordId: '001xx000003DGb2AAG' })`
questions.explain: Test wire adapters remember the settings the component sent them. `getLastConfig()` returns the latest config, with `'$recordId'` already replaced by the real Id.
wrong: The component doesn't call the adapter like a function, so call checks don't apply.
`account` isn't `public`, so the test can't read it, and no data was emitted.
`emit()` is what the test calls to push data; it doesn't record the config.
questions.source: sfdx-lwc-jest test wire adapters (lwc-recipes apexWireMethodWithParams test)

questions.q: A Visualforce controller extension catches a `DmlException` in `save()` and calls `ApexPages.addMessages(e)`. The test below forces the failure. Which assertion best proves that the user would see an error on the page?
options: `Assert.isNull(next)`, because a null `PageReference` always means an error message was shown
`Assert.isTrue(ApexPages.hasMessages(ApexPages.Severity.ERROR))`
`Assert.areEqual(1, [SELECT COUNT() FROM ApexPageMessage__c])`
`Assert.isTrue(Test.isRunningTest())`
questions.explain: Check the messages the page would show, not a side effect. `ApexPages.hasMessages(ApexPages.Severity.ERROR)` proves an error was added. `ApexPages.getMessages()` reads the messages.
wrong: A null return just keeps the user on the page; it doesn't prove a message.
Page messages aren't saved as records.
That only proves the code runs in a test.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: ApexPages Class

questions.q: Users report a JavaScript error in a Lightning web component in a sandbox. In the browser's developer tools, the framework and component code is minified and hard to follow. Which two actions help the developer debug the component's JavaScript? (Choose 2)
options: Set the Apex Code log level to `FINEST` for the user
Enable Debug Mode for the developer's user in Setup so Lightning JavaScript isn't minified
Run the component's Jest tests against the sandbox with `--target-org`
Open a downloaded debug log in Apex Replay Debugger to step through the component's JavaScript
Add a `debugger` statement or set a breakpoint in the browser's Sources panel, then reproduce the issue
questions.explain: To debug browser JavaScript, make it readable and then pause it. Debug Mode serves Lightning JavaScript unminified. A breakpoint or `debugger` statement then pauses the code in the browser's developer tools.
wrong: Debug logs cover server-side code, not JavaScript in the browser.
Jest tests run locally in Node.js and never connect to an org.
Replay Debugger replays Apex from logs, not browser JavaScript.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Debug Lightning Web Components; Salesforce Help: Enable Debug Mode for Lightning Components

questions.q: An import utility logs its failures to a custom object. During a large import, users get an error and no `Import_Log__c` record is written, and the debug log shows no "Import finished" line. What explains this?
options: The `catch` block runs, but its insert is rolled back because DML inside a `try` statement only commits on success
A `QueryException` is thrown first, and `catch (Exception e)` can't catch it
The 101st query throws `System.LimitException`, which can't be caught, so the whole transaction rolls back
The `finally` block runs first and ends the transaction before `catch` can log
questions.explain: Hitting a governor limit is a crash you can't catch. The 101st query throws `System.LimitException`, so `catch` and `finally` don't run and the transaction rolls back. Bulkify the query, or check `Limits.getQueries()` first.
wrong: For catchable exceptions, the `catch` block runs and its DML commits.
`QueryException` is catchable with `catch (Exception e)`.
`finally` runs after `catch`, and it doesn't end the transaction.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Exception Statements

questions.q: A support engineer chasing an intermittent bug leaves `FINEST` logging on for an integration user that runs all day. Which two statements about debug log limits are correct? (Choose 2)
options: A log larger than 20 MB is reduced by removing older log lines, which can come from anywhere in the log
A log larger than 20 MB is discarded completely and replaced by a single entry saying the log was too large
While the Developer Console is open, debug logs are generated for every user in the org
If more than 1,000 MB of debug logs is generated in 15 minutes, trace flags are disabled
System debug logs are kept for 30 days
questions.explain: Debug logs have size and time caps. A log over 20 MB is trimmed by removing older lines, and over 1,000 MB of logs in 15 minutes switches trace flags off. System debug logs are kept for 24 hours.
wrong: The log is trimmed, not thrown away.
The Developer Console records logs only for its own user.
System debug logs are kept for 24 hours; monitoring debug logs for seven days.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Debug Log

questions.q: An integration user calls `OrderService` through a REST endpoint. To get detail from that class only, a developer adds an Apex class trace flag on `OrderService` with Apex Code set to `FINEST`, then waits. No debug logs appear for the integration calls. What should the developer do?
options: Add `System = FINEST` to the class trace flag's debug level
Add a trigger trace flag on every trigger that `OrderService` fires
Keep the Developer Console open while the calls run, because it records logs for every user while it's open
Add a user trace flag for the integration user; class trace flags don't start logging on their own
questions.explain: A class trace flag sets the detail, but it doesn't switch logging on. A user trace flag on the integration user starts the logs. The class flag then sets the detail for `OrderService`.
wrong: More categories on the class flag still don't start logging.
Trigger trace flags don't start logs on their own either.
The Developer Console records logs only for its own user.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Debug Log

questions.q: After a release, updating 120 Opportunities with Data Loader fails. The developer pulls this excerpt from the debug log. What is the root cause?
questions.code:
13:02:11.204 (204511000)|CODE_UNIT_STARTED|[EXTERNAL]|01qxx0000004C9z|OpportunityTrigger on Opportunity trigger event AfterUpdate
13:02:11.209 (209881000)|SOQL_EXECUTE_BEGIN|[14]|Aggregations:0|SELECT Id, Rating FROM Account WHERE Id = :tmpVar1
13:02:11.212 (212004000)|SOQL_EXECUTE_END|[14]|Rows:1
13:02:11.215 (215120000)|SOQL_EXECUTE_BEGIN|[14]|Aggregations:0|SELECT Id, Rating FROM Account WHERE Id = :tmpVar1
13:02:11.217 (217337000)|SOQL_EXECUTE_END|[14]|Rows:1
... the same pair repeats, always at line [14] ...
13:02:11.871 (871220000)|EXCEPTION_THROWN|[14]|System.LimitException: Too many SOQL queries: 101
13:02:11.871 (871390000)|FATAL_ERROR|System.LimitException: Too many SOQL queries: 101
options: Data Loader sends 1,000 records per trigger call, which lowers the query limit
Line 14 runs an Account query per Opportunity inside a loop. Query once with a set of Ids before it
The Account query isn't selective, so it times out and is retried automatically until the SOQL limit is hit
The trigger should catch the `LimitException` and retry the remaining records in a Queueable
questions.explain: The same line running the same query again and again means a query inside a loop. Every `SOQL_EXECUTE_BEGIN` comes from line [14], with one row each time. Query once with `WHERE Id IN :accountIds` before the loop.
wrong: Triggers get records in chunks of up to 200, and the limit stays the same.
Each query returns one row in milliseconds; nothing times out.
`LimitException` can't be caught.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Debug Log; Execution Governors and Limits

questions.q: A nightly batch job should create a follow-up Task for each Opportunity. The job completes, no exception appears in the debug log, but many Tasks are missing. What is the most likely cause?
options: With `allOrNone` `false`, failed records are returned in SaveResults instead of throwing, and nobody checks them
Tasks inserted in `execute()` are held until `finish()` runs, and they're dropped if `finish()` doesn't commit them
DML in `execute()` is deferred to the next `execute()` call, so records from the last chunk are never saved
`WhatId` can't be set from Apex, so those Tasks are skipped
questions.explain: With `allOrNone` set to `false`, failures don't throw; they hide in the results. Failed records, for example ones with an inactive owner, appear only in the returned `Database.SaveResult` list. Check `isSuccess()` and log `getErrors()`.
wrong: Records inserted in `execute()` commit when that `execute()` transaction ends.
DML isn't held over between `execute()` calls.
Apex can set `WhatId` on a Task.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: Database Class; SaveResult Class

questions.q: A CI script builds an unlocked package version. The pipeline owner wants fast builds, but the version must be promotable to released. The command below fails right away. Why?
questions.code:
sf package version create \
  --package "Billing Core" \
  --installation-key-bypass \
  --skip-validation \
  --code-coverage \
  --wait 30
options: `--installation-key-bypass` can't be used with unlocked packages, so the version needs an `--installation-key`
`--skip-validation` can't be combined with `--code-coverage`, and skip-validation versions can't be promoted
`--wait` must be at least 60 minutes when `--code-coverage` is set
Unlocked packages compute coverage at promote time, so `--code-coverage` isn't a valid flag
questions.explain: Coverage is measured during validation, so you can't skip one and keep the other. `--skip-validation` and `--code-coverage` can't be combined. Versions built with skip validation also can't be promoted.
wrong: Installation key bypass is valid for unlocked packages.
There's no minimum wait time.
Coverage is measured at version creation with `--code-coverage`, and promotion needs it.
questions.source: Salesforce DX Developer Guide: Create New Versions of an Unlocked Package; Code Coverage for Unlocked Packages

questions.q: A release manager is planning environments for a regulated insurer. Which two statements about sandboxes are correct? (Choose 2)
options: A Developer sandbox includes a sample of production data chosen by a sandbox template
A Partial Copy sandbox copies all production data but no metadata
A Developer Pro sandbox can be refreshed once a day
Refreshing a sandbox keeps the sandbox's own changes and adds production's new metadata
A Full sandbox can be refreshed every 29 days
questions.explain: Each sandbox type has its own refresh interval. Developer and Developer Pro refresh every day, and Full every 29 days. Only Partial Copy and Full sandboxes copy production data.
wrong: Developer sandboxes copy metadata only; templates are for Partial Copy and Full.
Partial Copy copies all metadata plus a template-picked sample of data.
A refresh replaces the sandbox with a new copy, so its own changes are lost.
questions.source: Salesforce Help: Sandbox Types and Templates

questions.q: A release pipeline must read per-class coverage after tests run in a sandbox, to block merges below 85%. The command below fails with sObject type `'ApexCodeCoverageAggregate'` is not supported. What is the fix?
questions.code:
sf data query \
  --query "SELECT ApexClassOrTrigger.Name, NumLinesCovered, NumLinesUncovered FROM ApexCodeCoverageAggregate" \
  --target-org uat
options: Add `--use-tooling-api`, because `ApexCodeCoverageAggregate` is a Tooling API object
Retrieve `ApexCodeCoverageAggregate` with `sf project retrieve start`, because it is Metadata API metadata
Run the query in Execute Anonymous, because coverage records are only visible from Apex
Query a coverage field on `ApexClass` through the standard API instead
questions.explain: Coverage records live in the Tooling API, not the standard API. `ApexCodeCoverageAggregate` is a Tooling API object, so `sf data query` needs `--use-tooling-api`.
wrong: Coverage results aren't metadata, so they can't be retrieved.
Apex SOQL can't query Tooling API objects.
`ApexClass` has no coverage field; coverage lives in Tooling API objects.
questions.source: Tooling API Developer Guide: ApexCodeCoverageAggregate; Salesforce CLI Command Reference: data query

questions.q: A team that relies heavily on admins is moving from change sets to DevOps Center. Which statement describes how DevOps Center manages changes?
options: It packages each work item into an outbound change set and uploads it to the next connected org in the pipeline
It requires every developer to work in scratch orgs created from a Dev Hub
Work items are committed to a source control repository and promoted through pipeline stages
It lets work items skip Apex tests when they are promoted to production
questions.explain: DevOps Center is built on source control. Each work item's changes are committed to a repository and promoted through pipeline stages, instead of moving by change set.
wrong: DevOps Center replaces change sets with promotion based on source control.
Sandboxes work as development environments; scratch orgs aren't required.
Production deploys still follow the normal Apex test rules.
questions.source: Salesforce Help: DevOps Center

questions.q: Before a release, a developer wants to check that the changes deploy cleanly to the UAT sandbox, including running local tests, without changing UAT. The team lead says the command below is the wrong tool for a sandbox. Which command should the developer use?
questions.code: sf project deploy validate --source-dir force-app --target-org uat
options: `sf project deploy start --source-dir force-app --target-org uat --test-level RunLocalTests --ignore-conflicts`
`sf project deploy quick --source-dir force-app --target-org uat`
`sf project deploy preview --source-dir force-app --target-org uat`
`sf project deploy start --source-dir force-app --target-org uat --dry-run --test-level RunLocalTests`
questions.explain: To test-drive a deploy to a sandbox, use a dry run. `deploy validate` is meant for production, so the CLI reference recommends `deploy start --dry-run` with a test level. It validates and runs the tests but saves nothing.
wrong: Without `--dry-run`, this really deploys and changes UAT.
`quick` deploys an earlier validation by job ID; it doesn't validate source.
`preview` only lists what would deploy and possible conflicts; it runs no tests.
questions.source: Salesforce CLI Command Reference: project deploy validate

questions.q: A validation against production succeeded on Monday morning. On Saturday the release manager runs the command below, and it reports that no validated deployment was found. Nothing else has been validated since Monday. What should they do?
questions.code: sf project deploy quick --use-most-recent --target-org prod
options: Validate again, because a validated job ID expires after 3 days
Pass the job ID with `--job-id`. It stays valid for 10 days, but `--use-most-recent` only looks back 3 days
Add `--test-level RunLocalTests` so quick deploy can run the tests again
Run `sf project deploy resume --use-most-recent`, which turns the most recent validation into a deployment
questions.explain: The job ID lasts longer than the shortcut that finds it. `--use-most-recent` only looks back 3 days. The job ID itself is valid for 10 days from the start of validation, so pass it with `--job-id`.
wrong: The job ID is valid for 10 days; only `--use-most-recent` is limited to 3.
Quick deploy skips tests because they already ran during validation.
`resume` watches an operation that is still running; it doesn't deploy a validation.
questions.source: Salesforce CLI Command Reference: project deploy quick

questions.q: The custom field `Account.Legacy_Code__c` is referenced by the Apex class `AccountMapper`. The team wants one deployment that updates `AccountMapper` to remove the reference and also deletes the field. In which manifest should the field be listed?
questions.code:
<!-- package.xml -->
<Package xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata">
  <types>
    <members>AccountMapper</members>
    <name>ApexClass</name>
  </types>
  <version>62.0</version>
</Package>

<!-- deletion manifest: which file? -->
<Package xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata">
  <types>
    <members>Account.Legacy_Code__c</members>
    <name>CustomField</name>
  </types>
</Package>
options: `destructiveChangesPre.xml`, so the field is deleted before the class is compiled
`package.xml`, with a delete flag on the members element
`destructiveChangesPost.xml`, so the field is deleted after `AccountMapper` is updated
`destructiveChanges.xml` with `<members>*</members>` to remove every unused field
questions.explain: Remove the reference first, then delete the field. `destructiveChangesPost.xml` deletes after the other components deploy, so `AccountMapper` drops its reference first. Post-destructive changes are still processed before tests run.
wrong: Deleting first fails, because the current `AccountMapper` still uses the field.
`package.xml` has no delete option; deletions go in a destructive changes manifest.
Wildcards aren't allowed there, and plain `destructiveChanges.xml` deletes before additions.
questions.source: Metadata API Developer Guide: Deleting Components from an Organization

questions.q: A team is writing CI rules for `sf project deploy start`. Which two statements about test levels are correct? (Choose 2)
options: `RunAllTestsInOrg` skips tests that come from installed managed packages
`NoTestRun` applies only to development environments such as sandboxes, Developer Edition and trial orgs
With `RunSpecifiedTests`, the deployment passes as long as org-wide coverage stays at 75%, whatever each class reaches
`RunLocalTests` runs every test in the org except tests from installed managed and unlocked packages
`sf project deploy validate` defaults to `NoTestRun` unless `--test-level` is set
questions.explain: Each test level has a clear scope. `NoTestRun` is only for development environments, and `RunLocalTests` skips tests from installed managed and unlocked packages. `RunSpecifiedTests` needs 75% per class and trigger, and `deploy validate` defaults to `RunLocalTests`.
wrong: `RunAllTestsInOrg` includes managed package tests.
`RunSpecifiedTests` needs 75% coverage for each class and trigger deployed.
`deploy validate` requires tests and defaults to `RunLocalTests`.
questions.source: Salesforce CLI Command Reference: project deploy start; project deploy validate

questions.q: `QuoteService` gets a `Notifier` through its constructor. A test must prove that `submit()` calls `Notifier.send` exactly once with the quote's Id, without sending anything. What should the test do?
options: Call `Test.createStub`, then use `Test.verify(stub, 'send', 1)` after `submit()` to check the calls the stub received
Stub `Notifier` with `Test.createStub`; in `handleMethodCall`, record each method name and args, then assert
Call `Test.setMock(Notifier.class, new NotifierMock())` and read `Limits.getCallouts()` afterwards to count sends
Subclass `Notifier` in the test class, redeclare `send()` as `static`, and check a `static` counter after `submit()`
questions.explain: A stub can count its own calls, because every call passes through it. `handleMethodCall` gets the method name and `listOfArgs`, so record them and assert. The Stub API has no built-in verify.
wrong: There is no `Test.verify`; the provider must record the calls itself.
`Test.setMock` is only for callout mocks, and `send()` makes no callout to count.
An instance method can't be redeclared as `static`, and statics can't be stubbed anyway.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Build a Mocking Framework with the Stub API; StubProvider Interface

questions.q: A developer wrote a `StubProvider` for `TaxService` but can't make `InvoiceBuilder` use it in a test. What change makes the stub usable?
options: Make `TaxService.calculate` `static`, so that `Test.createStub` can replace it for the whole transaction
Annotate `TaxService` with `@TestVisible`, so `Test.createStub` swaps every `new TaxService()` in tests
Call `Test.setMock(TaxService.class, stub)` first, so `new TaxService()` returns the stub instead
Have `InvoiceBuilder` accept a `TaxService` in its constructor, defaulting to `new TaxService()`
questions.explain: The Stub API makes a stub object; it doesn't intercept `new`. The class under test needs a seam, such as constructor injection, so the test can pass the stub in.
wrong: Static methods can't be stubbed with the Stub API.
`@TestVisible` only exposes private members to tests; it doesn't redirect `new`.
`Test.setMock` only works for callout mocks, not for Apex classes.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Build a Mocking Framework with the Stub API

questions.q: With Debug Mode on, a developer logs `this.order` (an `@api` object) from an LWC. Chrome's console shows a Proxy instead of the order's fields. How can they see the real values without changing how the component behaves?
options: Turn off Lightning Web Security in Session Settings, because LWS wraps every `@api` object in its own Proxy
Remove `@api` from `order` while debugging, because the engine wraps only public properties in proxies
Turn on Enable custom formatters in the DevTools Console settings to see the values inside LWC proxies
Turn off secure and persistent browser caching, so the console receives the unwrapped objects instead
questions.explain: A DevTools setting can unwrap LWC proxies for you. Turn on Enable custom formatters in the Console settings. The LWC formatter shows the real values and leaves the proxies in place; with LWS on, it adds extra messages too.
wrong: The proxies come from the LWC engine, not LWS, and turning off security changes behavior.
Changing the decorator changes the component, and tracked objects are proxied too.
Browser caching affects which code loads, not how objects show in the console.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Debug Using Chrome DevTools

questions.q: In a sandbox, a developer deploys LWC fixes several times a day. After each deploy, reloading the record page often runs the old JavaScript until they empty the browser cache. What does Salesforce recommend?
options: Enable Debug Mode for every user in the sandbox, because debug mode turns off all caching of component code
Add a version query string to the component's import statements, so that each deploy produces a brand-new module URL
Set `cacheable=false` on the component's Apex methods, because cacheable responses keep the old component code
Clear Enable secure and persistent browser caching in Session Settings while debugging, then turn it back on
questions.explain: Browser caching can keep old component code around. In a sandbox or Developer Edition org, clear Enable secure and persistent browser caching while you debug. It hurts performance badly, so turn it back on after, and keep it on in production.
wrong: Debug Mode serves unminified code; it's not the documented fix for stale cached components.
LWC module imports don't take query strings; the platform serves component code.
Apex caching affects data responses, not the component's JavaScript.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Disable Caching During Development

questions.q: An LWC error is caught by framework code, so the console shows only a generic message and the stack points into framework files. How can the developer find the line in their own code that throws?
options: In the Chrome DevTools Sources panel, turn on pause on exceptions and then reproduce the error
Set the Apex Code and Visualforce log levels to `FINEST` and read the JavaScript stack in the log
Wrap the LWC in an Aura component, because Aura prints the full JavaScript stack for children
Run the component's Jest tests with `--coverage`, which records the line where the browser failed
questions.explain: Pausing on exceptions stops the browser at the line that throws. That works even if framework code catches the error later. So you land on the failing line in your own source.
wrong: Debug logs record server-side activity, not browser JavaScript stacks.
Wrapping in Aura doesn't change where the exception is caught.
Jest coverage measures local test runs, not errors in the browser.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Debug Using Chrome DevTools

questions.q: A Jest test for an LWC fails. The developer wants to step through the test and the component's event handler with breakpoints in Chrome DevTools. What should they do?
options: Deploy the component with its `__tests__` folder to a sandbox and run it from the Developer Console
Run `npm run test:unit:debug` (`sfdx-lwc-jest --debug`), then open `chrome://inspect` and pick the Jest process
Enable Debug Mode for the user, then open the Lightning page in Chrome so that the Jest test runs in its console
Add `console.log` calls to the test and run `sf apex run test --synchronous` to read them in the debug log
questions.explain: Jest has a debug mode that Chrome can attach to. `sfdx-lwc-jest --debug` runs Jest under `node --inspect-brk`, and `chrome://inspect` lists the process for DevTools. VS Code's Debug Test link does the same.
wrong: Jest tests run locally in Node.js, not in an org.
Debug Mode affects code served by the org; Jest tests never run there.
`sf apex run test` runs Apex tests, not Jest tests.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Debug Jest Tests for Lightning Web Components

questions.q: A test for a quote calculator inserts a `Product2` and a custom `Pricebook2`, then inserts a `PricebookEntry` for the custom price book. The insert fails with `STANDARD_PRICE_NOT_DEFINED`. The class does not use `SeeAllData`. What should the test do?
options: Add `@IsTest(SeeAllData=true)` to the class, because the standard price book can only be read from org data
First insert a `PricebookEntry` for the same product with `Pricebook2Id = Test.getStandardPricebookId()`
Insert a new `Pricebook2` with `IsStandard = true`, then add the product's standard price to that price book
Query `[SELECT Id FROM Pricebook2 WHERE IsStandard = true]`, which tests can always see without `SeeAllData`
questions.explain: A product needs a standard price before it can have a custom price. `Test.getStandardPricebookId()` gives the standard price book's Id in any test, with no org data. Insert the standard entry first, then the custom one.
wrong: Org data isn't needed; a `Test` method gives you the Id.
`IsStandard` is read-only, so a test can't make a second standard price book.
Without `SeeAllData`, that query finds no rows in a test.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: Test Class (getStandardPricebookId); Apex Developer Guide: Isolation of Test Data from Organization Data

questions.q: A discount service reads `Discount_Rule__mdt` records and the hierarchy custom setting `Pricing_Config__c`. A new test class has no `SeeAllData`. Which two statements are true? (Choose 2)
options: The test can read the org's `Pricing_Config__c` values without creating them
The test can read the org's `Discount_Rule__mdt` records without creating them
The test can create `Discount_Rule__mdt` records with a normal `insert` statement
Neither type is visible, so both must be loaded with `Test.loadData()` from a static resource
The test must insert the `Pricing_Config__c` record it needs before calling the service
questions.explain: Custom metadata records are metadata, so tests can read them. Custom setting records are data, so a test sees none unless it inserts them. Think: metadata comes along, data stays home.
wrong: Custom setting values are data, and tests don't see org data by default.
Apex can't insert custom metadata records with DML.
Custom metadata is already visible, and a custom setting can simply be inserted.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Isolation of Test Data from Organization Data; Custom Metadata Types Implementation Guide

questions.q: A team's `TestDataFactory` is a normal `public` class. It counts toward the org's Apex code size limit and lowers the coverage numbers. How should they change it so every test class can still call it?
options: Make it `private` and annotate it `@IsTest`, then call it from each test class as `TestDataFactory.createAccounts()`
Move the helper methods into a `@TestSetup` method in each test class, then delete the shared factory class
Mark the class `@TestVisible`, which hides it from coverage and the size limit but still lets tests call it
Annotate the class `@IsTest` and keep it and its helper methods `public`, so other test classes can call them
questions.explain: Code in a `@IsTest` class doesn't count toward the Apex code size limit or coverage. Its `public` methods can still be called from other test classes. So the factory keeps working and stops costing you.
wrong: A `private` test class can't be called from other classes.
That copies the same setup into many classes instead of sharing one factory.
`@TestVisible` opens private members to tests; it doesn't exclude a class from limits.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Common Test Utility Classes for Test Data Creation; IsTest Annotation

questions.q: A test inserts Accounts named `Alpha`, `Beta` and `Gamma`, then queries `[SELECT Name FROM Account]` and asserts that row 0 is `Alpha`. It passes locally but fails now and then in CI. What is the best fix?
options: Insert the Accounts one at a time, so that their creation order becomes the query order
Keep `@IsTest(isParallel=false)` on the class, because parallel runs shuffle query rows
Add `ORDER BY Name` to the query, since SOQL returns rows in no fixed order without it
Wrap the query in `Test.startTest()` and `Test.stopTest()` so the insert finishes first
questions.explain: SOQL doesn't promise any row order unless you ask for one. Add `ORDER BY` whenever a test reads rows by position. Then the result is the same on every run.
wrong: Insert order still doesn't fix the order a query returns.
Running tests one at a time doesn't give a query a fixed order.
The insert has already finished; `startTest()` resets limits and collects async work.
questions.source: SOQL and SOSL Reference: ORDER BY

questions.q: A factory method creates a test User with `Username = 'agent@acme.test'`. The tests pass in one sandbox but fail with `DUPLICATE_USERNAME` in another org. What is the cause and the fix?
options: Usernames are unique across all Salesforce orgs, so build each one from a random or time value
Test Users stay in the org after a run, so delete them in a `@TestSetup` method before each test class
That sandbox already has a real user with this name, so add `SeeAllData=false` to hide the real user
The `Email` value must differ from the `Username`, so give the test user a separate email address
questions.explain: A username must be unique across every Salesforce org, not just yours. Test inserts roll back, but this check still runs. So build usernames that can't clash, for example with a timestamp or the org Id.
wrong: Test data is rolled back after each test, so the User doesn't stay.
`SeeAllData` controls what a test can query, not the username check.
Email and Username may be the same value; that's not the error.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Using the runAs Method (creating test users); Salesforce Help: Usernames

questions.q: A shared helper `TestUtil.runJob()` calls `Test.startTest()`, enqueues a job and calls `Test.stopTest()`. A test method calls `Test.startTest()` itself and then calls `TestUtil.runJob()`. What happens?
options: The job runs twice, once for each `Test.startTest()` call, and the test checks doubled results
The inner calls are ignored, and all async work runs at the outer `Test.stopTest()` instead
The test fails, because each test method may call `Test.startTest()` only once
Governor limits reset a second time, which hides a limit problem but lets the test pass
questions.explain: A test method gets one `Test.startTest()` and one `Test.stopTest()`. A second call is an error, so the test fails. Keep the start and stop calls in the test method, not in shared helpers.
wrong: There is no second run; the second `startTest()` call is an error.
Nested calls aren't merged; the platform rejects the second one.
Limits don't reset again; the second call fails first.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Using Limits, startTest, and stopTest

questions.q: A batch class sets `Status__c = 'Done'` on a `Job_Run__c` record in its `finish()` method. Its test, below, queries that record right after `Test.stopTest()`. What does the test see?
options: `null`, because `finish()` is queued as a separate job that runs only after the test has ended
`'Done'`, because `start()`, `execute()` and `finish()` all run when `Test.stopTest()` is called
`'Done'` only if the test passes `Database.Stateful` to `Database.executeBatch()` as an argument
An error, because `Test.stopTest()` can't run a batch that updates records outside its own scope
questions.explain: `Test.stopTest()` makes queued async work finish right away. For a batch, that means `start()`, `execute()` and `finish()` all run. So the record shows `'Done'` after `stopTest()`.
wrong: `finish()` runs at `stopTest()` together with the rest of the batch.
`Database.Stateful` is an interface on the class, not an argument.
A batch may update any records; `stopTest()` just runs it.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing Batch Apex

questions.q: A test schedules `WeeklyDigest` with `System.schedule('Digest', '0 0 6 ? * MON', new WeeklyDigest())` and keeps the returned Id. Before `Test.stopTest()`, how can it prove the job was scheduled correctly?
options: Call `new WeeklyDigest().execute(null)` and assert that it returns the job's next fire time
Read `Limits.getScheduledJobs()`, which returns each scheduled job's cron expression as text
Assert on the value from `System.schedule()`, which is the next fire time as a `Datetime`
Query `CronTrigger` by that Id and assert its `CronExpression`, and that `TimesTriggered` is 0
questions.explain: `System.schedule()` returns the Id of a `CronTrigger` record. Query it to check `CronExpression`, `NextFireTime` and `TimesTriggered`. Before `stopTest()` the job hasn't run, so `TimesTriggered` is 0.
wrong: `execute()` returns nothing and doesn't report schedule details.
There's no such `Limits` method; limits report counts, not schedules.
It returns the job's Id, not a fire time.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing the Apex Scheduler

questions.q: An after-insert trigger on `Order__c` calls a `@future(callout=true)` method that posts the order to an ERP. The test below fails with an error saying test methods don't support callouts. What should change?
options: Call `Test.setMock()` before `Test.stopTest()`, because the future method's callout runs at `stopTest()`
Remove `Test.startTest()` and `Test.stopTest()`, so that the future method runs after the assertion
Change the method to `@future(callout=false)` while testing, then switch it back before deploying
Move `insert o;` above `Test.startTest()`, so the trigger and its callout run outside the test context
questions.explain: A mock must be in place before the callout runs. The future method runs at `Test.stopTest()`, which here comes before `Test.setMock()`. Register the mock first, then stop the test.
wrong: Removing them doesn't add a mock, so the callout still has nothing to answer it.
Changing code for tests hides real behavior, and the callout would then be blocked.
Moving the insert doesn't register a mock before the callout runs.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing HTTP Callouts; Testing Future Methods

questions.q: A `without sharing` class `ReportService` returns Opportunities. A test calls it inside `System.runAs(repUser)`, and `repUser` can see only their own 2 Opportunities. The test expects 2 rows but gets 50. Why?
options: `runAs` never applies record sharing; it only changes the value of `UserInfo.getUserId()`
Code in `ReportService` runs in that class's own sharing mode, which `runAs` doesn't override
The test also needs `SeeAllData=true`, so `runAs` can load the sharing rules for `repUser`
`repUser` was inserted in the same test, and new users get View All Data until the test ends
questions.explain: Inside `runAs`, the sharing mode comes from the class where the code is written. `ReportService` is `without sharing`, so it sees every record. Only code that runs with sharing applies `repUser`'s record access.
wrong: `runAs` does apply the user's record sharing to code that runs with sharing.
`SeeAllData` is about org data, not sharing rules.
New test users get only what their profile and sharing give them.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Using the runAs Method

questions.q: A sandbox has no spare Salesforce user licenses. A test inserts a new User with a Salesforce profile and runs code inside `System.runAs(newUser)`. What happens?
options: The insert fails with a license error, so tests must reuse an existing active user in the org
The test runs only if the User is created inside another `runAs` block for an existing admin
The test runs, because `runAs` ignores user license limits, so tests can create users freely
The test runs, but the user acts as Chatter Free, so object permissions are ignored for it
questions.explain: Tests may create users even when the org has no spare licenses. The `runAs` docs say it ignores user license limits. So build the users you need inside the test.
wrong: License limits don't block test users created for `runAs`.
No extra `runAs` wrapper is needed to insert the user.
The user keeps the profile and license you gave it.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Using the runAs Method

questions.q: `OrderService` has `private static Integer retryLimit = 3;` and a `private` method `buildPayload()`. A test must set `retryLimit` to 1 and call `buildPayload()` directly. Which two statements are true? (Choose 2)
options: Annotating both members with `@TestVisible` lets test code read, set and call them
Test classes can already reach `private` members of any class in the same namespace
`@TestVisible` also makes the members visible to non-test classes in the same org
The members stay `private` for normal code; only test code gets the extra access
The test must be an inner class of `OrderService` to call `buildPayload()`, even with `@TestVisible`
questions.explain: `@TestVisible` opens `private` and `protected` members to test code only. Normal code still sees them as `private`. So the test can set `retryLimit` and call `buildPayload()` directly.
wrong: Without `@TestVisible`, `private` members are hidden from tests too.
Only test code gets access; other classes still can't see them.
With `@TestVisible`, any test class can call the method.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: TestVisible Annotation

questions.q: A test must confirm that `PaymentService.charge()` throws `PaymentService.CardDeclinedException` and not some other error. The `try` block calls `charge()` and then `Assert.fail()`. Which `catch` block checks this best?
options: `catch (Exception e) { Assert.isTrue(e.getMessage().contains('Exception'), 'wrong error'); }`
`catch (Exception e) { Assert.areEqual('CardDeclinedException', e.getTypeName(), 'wrong error'); }`
`catch (Exception e) { Assert.isNotNull(e, 'An exception was expected but none was thrown'); }`
`catch (Exception e) { Assert.isInstanceOfType(e, PaymentService.CardDeclinedException.class); }`
questions.explain: Catch the general type, then check the exact type. `Assert.isInstanceOfType()` fails if any other exception comes back. The `Assert.fail()` after the call covers the case where nothing is thrown.
wrong: A message can contain any words; this doesn't check the exception's type.
`getTypeName()` returns the full name, `PaymentService.CardDeclinedException`, so this fails on the right error.
Any exception passes this check, even the wrong one.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: Assert Class; Exception Class

questions.q: To stop tests from emailing customers, a developer wraps `Messaging.sendEmail(msgs)` in `if (!Test.isRunningTest())`. A reviewer rejects the change. Which statement explains why?
options: Tests never deliver email anyway, so the guard just hides the send code from tests and coverage
`Test.isRunningTest()` returns true in every sandbox, so emails would also stop during UAT testing
`Messaging.sendEmail()` fails in tests unless `SeeAllData=true` is set on the test class
The guard must be `Test.isRunningTest() == false`, since `!` isn't allowed on that method
questions.explain: Email sent from an Apex test is never delivered. So the guard protects nothing, and the real send code never runs in a test. Let the code send, and check it with `Limits.getEmailInvocations()`.
wrong: It returns true only while test code is running, not in every sandbox.
Sending email in a test works without org data.
`!` works on any `Boolean`, including this one.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: Test.isRunningTest; Apex Developer Guide: Testing Best Practices

questions.q: An `@AuraEnabled(continuation=true)` method returns a `Continuation` for a slow carrier API, and its callback `processResponse` parses the result. How should a test cover both methods?
options: Register an `HttpCalloutMock` with `Test.setMock()`, then call the action; the callback runs on its own afterwards
Call the action, then `Test.setContinuationResponse(label, res)`, then `Test.invokeContinuationMethod(ctrl, con)`
Call the action inside `Test.startTest()` and `Test.stopTest()`, which waits for the callback to finish running
Call `con.addHttpRequest()` with a fake endpoint, then call `processResponse()` directly with `null` as its state
questions.explain: Continuation callouts don't use a normal callout mock. Set a fake response for the request label with `Test.setContinuationResponse()`. Then `Test.invokeContinuationMethod()` runs the callback, so both methods are covered.
wrong: `HttpCalloutMock` doesn't answer `Continuation` requests, and the callback never runs.
`stopTest()` doesn't run Continuation callbacks.
That skips the real request label, so the callback isn't tested properly.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing Asynchronous Callouts (Continuation)

questions.q: A test must prove that `InvoiceSync.push()` sends a `POST` with a JSON body holding the invoice number. The callout's reply gives nothing useful to assert on. Where should the checks go?
options: After `Test.stopTest()`: read the sent request from `Test.getLastCallout()` and assert on its body
In a debug log: set Callout to `FINEST`, run the test, and check the logged body by hand each release
In `InvoiceSync`: add an `if (Test.isRunningTest())` block that saves the request in a static field
In the mock's `respond(HTTPRequest req)`: assert on `req.getMethod()` and `req.getBody()`, then reply
questions.explain: The mock receives the real request your code built. So assert on `req.getMethod()`, `req.getEndpoint()` or `req.getBody()` inside `respond()`. Or save the request on the mock and assert after the call.
wrong: There is no `Test.getLastCallout()` method.
Checking a log by hand isn't an automated test.
Test-only code in the class is the `Test.isRunningTest()` trap; the mock already sees the request.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing HTTP Callouts by Implementing the HttpCalloutMock Interface

questions.q: `RateClient.fetch()` should throw `RateClient.RateException` when the API answers with status 503. How does a test cover that path?
options: Point the Named Credential at an unused URL during the test run, so the real request fails with a 503
Call `Test.setMock(HttpCalloutMock.class, null)`, which makes every callout in the test return 503
Register a mock that returns an `HttpResponse` with `setStatusCode(503)`, then expect the error
Call `Test.setFixedSearchResults()` with an error record, so the callout layer returns a failure
questions.explain: A mock can return any status you like. Build an `HttpResponse`, call `setStatusCode(503)` and return it. Then assert that `RateException` is thrown.
wrong: Tests can't make real callouts, whatever the URL.
A `null` mock gives no response at all.
That method sets SOSL search results, not callout replies.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing HTTP Callouts by Implementing the HttpCalloutMock Interface

questions.q: A test uses `StaticResourceCalloutMock` to fake one REST endpoint. Which two statements about it are true? (Choose 2)
options: The mock compares the request's endpoint with the resource name and fails when they differ
The static resource must be a zip file holding one JSON file for each HTTP status code
`setStaticResource()` takes the static resource's name, and that file's content becomes the body
It can answer several endpoints in one test, since each `setStaticResource()` call adds a URL
`setStatusCode()` and `setHeader()` set the status and headers that the response returns
questions.explain: `StaticResourceCalloutMock` returns one fixed response. You name the static resource for the body and set the status and headers yourself. For several endpoints, use `MultiStaticResourceCalloutMock`.
wrong: It answers any endpoint; it doesn't compare URLs.
The resource is just the body, such as one JSON file.
That's `MultiStaticResourceCalloutMock`, which maps each endpoint to a resource.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing HTTP Callouts Using Static Resources

questions.q: A test registers the mock below with `Test.setMock(WebServiceMock.class, new TaxSoapMock())`. The WSDL2Apex client then fails with a null error when it reads the reply. What is wrong?
options: Put the reply in the map under the key `'response_x'`, not under `'response'`
`doInvoke` must return the response element instead of putting it into a map
It must be registered with `HttpCalloutMock.class`, because SOAP runs over HTTP
`rate` must be set on `request`, which the runtime copies into the client's reply
questions.explain: WSDL2Apex clients read the reply from the map key `'response_x'`. This mock used `'response'`, so the client finds nothing. Write `response.put('response_x', res);`.
wrong: `doInvoke` returns `void`; the reply goes into the map.
SOAP mocks implement `WebServiceMock` and register with `WebServiceMock.class`.
The request is what your code sent; the reply comes only from the map.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Test Web Service Callouts

questions.q: Given the stub provider and test code below, what are the values of `a`, `b` and `c`?
questions.explain: Every call on a stubbed object goes to `handleMethodCall()`. Only `available` with `'SKU-1'` returns 5. Every other call, including `reserved`, falls through to `return 0;`.
wrong: `'SKU-2'` fails the argument check, so `b` gets 0.
`reserved` fails the method name check, so `c` gets 0.
The provider handles `reserved` too and returns 0, not `null`.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Build a Mocking Framework with the Stub API

questions.q: A test stubs `TaxCalculator` with `Test.createStub()` and passes the stub into `InvoiceBuilder`. The stub answers `round()`, but the real tax rate logic still runs. Which line explains it?
options: `this.calc = calc;` copies the stub, so the builder ends up holding a real `TaxCalculator`
`TaxCalculator.rateFor('EU')` is a static call, which the Stub API can't replace
`calc.round(...)` must be cast to `(TaxCalculator)` again before the stub can answer it
`private TaxCalculator calc;` must be `@TestVisible`, or the stub can't be passed in
questions.explain: The Stub API replaces instance methods on the stubbed object only. `rateFor` is called as a static method on the class, so the real code runs. Make it an instance method and call it through `calc`.
wrong: Assigning keeps a reference to the same stub; nothing is copied.
The field already has the right type; no extra cast is needed.
The stub is passed in through the constructor, so visibility isn't the issue.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Build a Mocking Framework with the Stub API (Apex Stub API Limitations)

questions.q: When saving fails, the `orderForm` LWC dispatches a `ShowToastEvent` with variant `error`. How should its Jest test check that the toast was sent?
options: Query `document.body` for a `lightning-toast` element after the failure and check its `variant`
Spy on `window.alert` with `jest.spyOn()`, because toasts fall back to alerts in the Jest DOM
Mock `lightning/uiRecordApi`, because toast messages travel through Lightning Data Service
Listen for `'lightning__showtoast'` on the component, cause the failure, and assert on `event.detail`
questions.explain: In Jest, nothing draws a real toast. `ShowToastEvent` is just an event named `lightning__showtoast`. Listen for it on the component and check `event.detail.variant` and the message.
wrong: No toast element is drawn in Jest; only the event is fired.
Toasts don't fall back to alerts.
Toasts have nothing to do with Lightning Data Service.
questions.source: LWC Recipes (GitHub): Jest tests for ShowToastEvent; Unit Test Lightning Web Components (Trailhead)

questions.q: A Jest file has three tests that each append a `c-cart` element. The third test fails because `querySelectorAll('c-cart')` finds three carts. What is missing?
options: An `afterEach()` that removes all children of `document.body` and calls `jest.clearAllMocks()`
An `await Promise.resolve()` at the start of each test, so the earlier carts finish unmounting first
A `beforeAll()` that creates one shared `c-cart` element and reuses it for every test in the file
The `--runInBand` flag, because tests in one file share a DOM only when run in parallel workers
questions.explain: Jest keeps one DOM for all the tests in a file. So clean up after each test: remove the children of `document.body`. Resetting mocks there too keeps one test from leaking into the next.
wrong: Waiting doesn't remove elements; nothing unmounts them on its own.
Sharing one element makes tests depend on each other.
Tests in one file share a DOM however they run.
questions.source: Unit Test Lightning Web Components (Trailhead): Write a Jest Test

questions.q: `accountBanner` reads `this.recordId` in `connectedCallback()` to start loading. In the test below, the component never loads anything. What should change?
options: Add a second `await Promise.resolve()`, as `connectedCallback()` waits for two microtasks
Set `element.recordId` before `appendChild()`, because `connectedCallback()` runs on insert
Call `element.connectedCallback()` again after setting `recordId`, so it reads the new value
Use `element.setAttribute('record-id', ...)`, as `@api` values set from JavaScript are ignored
questions.explain: `connectedCallback()` runs the moment the element is inserted into the DOM. Here `recordId` is set after that, so the hook saw `undefined`. Set public properties before `appendChild()`.
wrong: The hook already ran without an Id; waiting longer doesn't rerun it.
Lifecycle hooks aren't public methods a test should call.
Setting `@api` properties in JavaScript works; the timing is the problem.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Lifecycle Hooks; Unit Test Lightning Web Components (Trailhead)

questions.q: `filterPanel` calls `publish(this.messageContext, FILTER_CHANNEL, { region })` when a region is picked. How should its Jest test check this?
options: Add a second component that subscribes to `FILTER_CHANNEL` and assert that its region changes
Listen on `document` for a `CustomEvent` named `FILTER_CHANNEL` and assert on its `detail`
Import `publish` from `lightning/messageService`, which is a Jest mock, and assert on its call
Deploy the message channel first, because Jest loads `lightning/messageService` from the org
questions.explain: sfdx-lwc-jest swaps `lightning/messageService` for a stub whose `publish` is a `jest.fn()`. Fire the pick, then check `expect(publish).toHaveBeenCalledWith(...)` with the channel and payload. No real message bus runs in Jest.
wrong: The Jest stub doesn't deliver messages between components.
Message service messages aren't DOM events.
Jest runs offline with stubs, not against the org.
questions.source: LWC Recipes (GitHub): lmsPublisherWebComponent Jest test; sfdx-lwc-jest stubs

questions.q: Clicking View in `caseTile` calls `this[NavigationMixin.Navigate]` with a `standard__recordPage` reference. How can a Jest test check which page it targets?
options: Assert that `window.location.href` changed to the record URL after the click resolves
Listen for a bubbling `navigate` `CustomEvent` from `caseTile` and read `detail.recordId`
Call `jest.useFakeTimers()`, because navigation runs after a timeout Jest must advance
Mock `lightning/navigation` so `Navigate` saves the page reference, then assert on it
questions.explain: In Jest, navigation can't really go anywhere. The usual pattern mocks `lightning/navigation`, so the mixin's `Navigate` saves the page reference it gets. The test then checks its `type`, `recordId` and `actionName`.
wrong: No real navigation happens in Jest, so the URL doesn't change.
`NavigationMixin` doesn't fire a DOM event you can listen for.
Navigation isn't timer-based, so there's nothing to advance.
questions.source: LWC Recipes (GitHub): navToRecord Jest test and jest-mocks/lightning/navigation

questions.q: A component that wires `getRecord` shows an error panel when the wire fails. How does a Jest test reach that branch?
options: Call `getRecord.error()` on the test wire adapter, wait a microtask, then look for the error panel
Call `getRecord.emit(null)`, because a `null` record is how the wire service reports a failure
Throw an `Error` inside `jest.mock('lightning/uiRecordApi')`, which makes every wire fail
Set `element.error = true` on the component, because wire results are public in Jest tests
questions.explain: The test wire adapter has an `error()` method that sends an error to the component. Call it, then `await Promise.resolve()` so the template redraws. Then check that the error panel shows.
wrong: `emit()` sends data; a `null` record isn't an error.
Throwing in the mock factory breaks the import, not the wire.
Wired properties aren't public, and this skips the real wire path.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Test Wire Service (emit and error); sfdx-lwc-jest

questions.q: A Visualforce custom controller's `save()` returns `new PageReference('/' + acct.Id)`. How should a test check that it sends the user to the new Account?
options: Call `Test.setCurrentPage()` after `save()` and assert on `ApexPages.currentPage().getUrl()`
Assert that `ctrl.save().getUrl()` is `'/'` plus the Account's Id, queried after the save
Check `ApexPages.hasMessages()`, which is true whenever an action returns a `PageReference`
Assert that `save()` returned `null`, because tests never follow redirects to other pages
questions.explain: An action method returns a `PageReference`, and the test can inspect it. Compare `getUrl()` with the URL you expect. Tests don't follow the redirect; they check where it points.
wrong: That sets the page yourself; it doesn't show where `save()` points.
Page messages report errors and info, not redirects.
The method returns the `PageReference` whether or not anything follows it.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Testing Custom Controllers and Controller Extensions

questions.q: A developer plans to use Apex Replay Debugger in VS Code for several bugs. Which two statements about it are true? (Choose 2)
options: It can replay a debug log from a scheduled Apex job, just like a log from Anonymous Apex
Trigger context variables like `Trigger.new` show only at checkpoints, not at ordinary breakpoints
It can replay several async debug logs as one session, in the order that the jobs ran
Uploaded checkpoints expire after 30 minutes, so start the session soon after uploading them
It supports conditional breakpoints and watch expressions, like a live debugger does
questions.explain: Replay Debugger replays one saved log, so it has limits. Trigger context variables aren't in logs, so they show only at checkpoints. Checkpoints expire after 30 minutes.
wrong: Logs from scheduled Apex can't be replayed.
You can replay only one debug log at a time.
It doesn't support conditional breakpoints or watch expressions.
questions.source: Salesforce Extensions for VS Code: Apex Replay Debugger (Considerations)

questions.q: An Apex trigger on `Payment_Event__e` sometimes fails. The developer sets trace flags on their own user and on the integration user that publishes the events, but no log shows the trigger. What should they do?
options: Turn on Debug Mode for the integration user, which adds event trigger lines to that user's logs
Keep the Developer Console open while events publish, because it then logs every trigger in the org
Set the trace flag's Apex Code level to `FINEST`, because event triggers log only at that level
Add a trace flag for the Automated Process entity, since platform event triggers run as it
questions.explain: Platform event triggers don't run as the user who published the event. They run as the Automated Process entity, unless a different run-as user is set. So add a trace flag for Automated Process.
wrong: Debug Mode is for Lightning component JavaScript, not Apex logs.
The console logs only the current user's activity.
The level isn't the issue; the trace flag is on the wrong entity.
questions.source: Platform Events Developer Guide: Debugging Platform Event Triggers

questions.q: A support admin runs a fix script in Anonymous Apex. It fails to compile with a field error, but the same code saved in a class compiles. The field exists. What is the likely cause?
options: Anonymous Apex always compiles against API version 20.0, which doesn't know newer fields
Anonymous Apex can't reference custom fields; it supports only standard fields and objects
Anonymous Apex runs as the current user, so it fails if the admin lacks access to that field
The script needs the `with sharing` keyword at the top, or the compiler blocks every field
questions.explain: Anonymous Apex runs as the person who runs it. It can fail to compile if the code uses objects or fields that person can't access. Saved classes don't have that check, so the same code compiles there.
wrong: Anonymous Apex uses a current API version, not 20.0.
Anonymous Apex can use custom fields and objects.
Sharing keywords don't apply to anonymous blocks and have nothing to do with compiling fields.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Anonymous Blocks

questions.q: A developer needs the debug log to show each SOQL query and DML statement, with the rows returned, but little else. Which log category should they raise while lowering the others?
options: Database, which logs SOQL, SOSL and DML events and their row counts
Apex Code, which logs every Apex statement and therefore every query
System, which logs calls to system methods such as the query functions
Apex Profiling, which logs each query's text and every row it returned
questions.explain: Each log category covers one kind of event. **Database** covers SOQL, SOSL and DML, including row counts. Apex Profiling gives totals and limit usage, not each query.
wrong: Apex Code logs code flow, which adds lots of noise you don't need.
System logs system method calls, not query events.
Profiling shows totals and limits, not each query's rows.
questions.source: Salesforce Help: Debug Log Categories and Levels

questions.q: A scheduled job sometimes throws an unhandled exception at night. The team wants the on-call alias, not only the developer who last changed the class, to get the error email. What should they do?
options: Make the alias's user the last person to modify the class, because only that user gets the email
Wrap the job in `try`/`catch` and call `System.debug(LoggingLevel.ERROR, e)` so Salesforce emails it
Add the alias on the Apex Exception Email page in Setup, which sends errors to extra addresses
Add a trace flag for the alias's user, because trace flags email a log whenever an exception occurs
questions.explain: By default, the error email goes to the developer who last changed the class or trigger. The **Apex Exception Email** page in Setup adds more recipients, even outside addresses. So add the on-call alias there.
wrong: Faking who last edited the class is a hack, and it drops the real developer.
Debug lines go to logs, not email, and catching the error stops the email.
Trace flags create logs; they don't send email.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Unhandled Exception Emails; Salesforce Help: Apex Exception Email

questions.q: Saving a record takes 9 seconds. The developer opens the debug log in the Developer Console and wants to see which code units and methods used the most time. Which Log Inspector panel fits?
options: Execution Log, filtered with Debug Only, which lists each method's duration in milliseconds
Execution Overview, whose Timeline and Executed Units tabs show the time each unit took
Checkpoints, which record how long each method ran between two separate heap dumps
Source, which colors each code line by how long that line took to run in the transaction
questions.explain: The Log Inspector has a panel for each question. **Execution Overview** shows how time and limits were spent. Its Timeline and Executed Units tabs point to the slowest code.
wrong: Debug Only shows `System.debug` lines, not timings.
Checkpoints capture heap snapshots, not durations.
Source shows the code and how often lines ran, not a timing map.
questions.source: Salesforce Help: Log Inspector (Developer Console)

questions.q: A feature will take three weeks to build, and the developer wants one scratch org for the whole time. What should they do when creating it?
options: Nothing; a scratch org stays active until someone runs `sf org delete scratch`
Add `--duration-days 21`, but only after enabling long-lived orgs in the sandbox settings
Make a new one every 7 days and copy data over with `sf data export tree`, as 7 is the maximum
Add `--duration-days 21`; scratch orgs last 7 days by default and up to 30 days
questions.explain: Scratch orgs are short-lived on purpose. They last 7 days unless you set `--duration-days`, which allows up to 30 days. So `--duration-days 21` covers the feature.
wrong: Scratch orgs expire on their own, after 7 days by default.
No extra setting is needed for up to 30 days.
The maximum is 30 days, not 7.
questions.source: Salesforce DX Developer Guide: Create Scratch Orgs

questions.q: A team's `force-app` folder holds some local helper files the org can't use. Deploys fail because the Salesforce CLI tries to deploy those files. What should the team do?
options: List the files in `.forceignore`, which the CLI skips for deploys and retrieves
List the files in `.gitignore`, which the CLI reads to decide what to deploy to the org
Add `--ignore-conflicts` to the deploy, which skips files that the org doesn't recognize
Rename the files with a `.local` suffix, which the CLI always treats as local-only files
questions.explain: `.forceignore` lists files the Salesforce CLI should leave out. A new project already ignores entries like `**/__tests__/**` and `**/jsconfig.json`. Add any other local-only files there.
wrong: `.gitignore` is for Git; the CLI uses `.forceignore`.
`--ignore-conflicts` is about source tracking conflicts, not unknown files.
The CLI has no such naming rule.
questions.source: Salesforce DX Developer Guide: How to Exclude Source When Syncing or Converting (.forceignore)

questions.q: A team keeps its project in source format. An admin must deploy a release with a Metadata API tool that needs metadata format and a `package.xml`. Which command prepares the files?
options: `sf project retrieve start --target-metadata-dir out`, which converts local files without an org
`sf project convert source --output-dir mdapi_out`, which writes metadata format with a `package.xml`
`sf project generate manifest`, which writes all the source files out again in metadata format
`sf project deploy start --dry-run`, which saves to disk the converted files it would have deployed
questions.explain: Source format and metadata format hold the same metadata in different layouts. `sf project convert source` turns source format into metadata format, with a `package.xml`. Then any Metadata API tool can deploy it.
wrong: Retrieve pulls metadata from an org; it doesn't convert local files.
That writes only a `package.xml`, not converted files.
A dry run validates against an org and saves no files.
questions.source: Salesforce CLI Command Reference: project convert source

questions.q: A team wants the Salesforce CLI to track their changes in Developer sandboxes the way it does in scratch orgs. Which two statements are true? (Choose 2)
options: It's switched on in production, on the Dev Hub page, for Developer and Developer Pro sandboxes
Full and Partial Copy sandboxes also get source tracking once the setting is turned on
Only sandboxes created or refreshed after the setting is turned on get source tracking
Source tracking needs a namespace registered in the Dev Hub before sandboxes can use it
Tracking starts in existing sandboxes as soon as the setting is saved, with no refresh
questions.explain: Source tracking in sandboxes is opt-in. Turn it on in production, on the Dev Hub page, for Developer and Developer Pro sandboxes. Then create or refresh the sandboxes to get it.
wrong: Only Developer and Developer Pro sandboxes support source tracking.
No namespace is needed for source tracking.
Existing sandboxes must be refreshed first.
questions.source: Salesforce DX Developer Guide: Enable Source Tracking in Sandboxes

questions.q: A company wants to ship its Apex and LWC as an unlocked package. The code uses many custom fields that will stay unpackaged in production for now, so version creation fails. What is the best option?
options: Switch to a second-generation managed package, which skips the dependency checks during creation
Add `--skip-validation` to each package version, then promote one of those versions to released
Use an org-dependent unlocked package (`--org-dependent`); its dependencies are checked at install
Deploy the fields to the Dev Hub org first, since package builds read their metadata from the Dev Hub
questions.explain: An org-dependent unlocked package can depend on metadata that already lives in the target org. Its dependencies are checked when you install it, not when you build it. So the unpackaged fields don't block the build.
wrong: Managed packages check dependencies too, and they need a namespace.
Versions built with `--skip-validation` can't be promoted.
Package builds use their own build org, not the Dev Hub's metadata.
questions.source: Salesforce DX Developer Guide: Org-Dependent Unlocked Packages

questions.q: A developer wants to deploy only the `OrderService` Apex class from a Salesforce DX project. Which two commands do that? (Choose 2)
options: `sf project deploy start --metadata OrderService.cls`
`sf project retrieve start --metadata ApexClass:OrderService`
`sf project deploy start --tests OrderService`
`sf project deploy start --metadata ApexClass:OrderService`
`sf project deploy start --source-dir force-app/main/default/classes/OrderService.cls`
questions.explain: `sf project deploy start` can deploy just what you name. Use `--metadata` with a type and a name, or `--source-dir` with a path. `ApexClass:OrderService` is the type-and-name form.
wrong: `--metadata` needs a type and name, like `ApexClass:OrderService`, not a file name.
Retrieve pulls from the org; it doesn't deploy.
`--tests` picks which tests run; it doesn't choose what to deploy.
questions.source: Salesforce CLI Command Reference: project deploy start

questions.q: A release to production uses the `RunLocalTests` test level. Which two conditions must hold for the deployment to succeed? (Choose 2)
options: Every class in the deployment must reach 75% coverage on its own
Every test that runs must pass
Org-wide Apex coverage must be at least 75%
Every trigger in the org must reach 75% coverage on its own
Tests from installed managed packages must pass as well
questions.explain: With `RunLocalTests`, all tests that run must pass, and the org as a whole needs 75% coverage. Each trigger needs some coverage, but not 75%. The per-class 75% rule belongs to `RunSpecifiedTests`.
wrong: That per-class rule applies to `RunSpecifiedTests`.
Triggers need at least some coverage, not 75% each.
`RunLocalTests` doesn't run managed package tests.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Deploying Apex; Metadata API Developer Guide: Running Tests in a Deployment

questions.q: When the whole test suite runs, several test classes fail with `UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW`. Each class passes when it runs alone. What is the quickest fix?
options: Add `FOR UPDATE` to every query in the tests, so each test waits for the others to release rows
Add `@IsTest(isParallel=true)` to the classes, so the platform gives each one its own data copy
Move the shared inserts into `@TestSetup`, which locks those records for the whole test run
Select Disable Parallel Apex Testing in Apex Test Execution options, so tests run one by one
questions.explain: Tests run in parallel by default, and parallel tests can fight over the same rows. **Disable Parallel Apex Testing** runs them one at a time, so the lock errors stop. It's slower, so fix shared data if you can.
wrong: `FOR UPDATE` adds locks; it doesn't stop tests from colliding.
`isParallel=true` asks for parallel runs, which is the cause.
`@TestSetup` data isn't locked, and the classes still run in parallel.
questions.source: Salesforce Help: Disable Parallel Apex Testing; Apex Developer Guide: Running Unit Test Methods

questions.q: A team wants to run the same 12 test classes after every change, from the Developer Console and from the CLI, without retyping the list. What should they create?
options: An Apex test suite, run from the console or with `sf apex run test --suite-names`
A `@TestSetup` class that calls the 12 classes' methods in order from one test method
A permission set that lists the 12 classes, then run tests for users assigned to it
A `package.xml` that lists the 12 classes, which `sf apex run test` reads by default
questions.explain: A **test suite** is a saved list of test classes. You build it once in the Developer Console and run it again anytime. The CLI runs it with `sf apex run test --suite-names`.
wrong: Test methods can't run other test classes like that.
Permission sets don't choose which tests run.
`sf apex run test` doesn't read `package.xml`.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Apex Test Suites; Salesforce CLI Command Reference: apex run test

questions.q: A deployment to production contains only page layouts and one custom field, and the command sets no test level. What happens?
options: All local tests run, because every production deployment uses `RunLocalTests` by default
No tests run, because local tests run by default only when Apex classes or triggers are included
The deploy fails, because a production deployment must always name an explicit test level
All tests in the org run, including managed package tests, because no Apex is being deployed
questions.explain: In production, the default test level depends on what you deploy. If the deployment has Apex classes or triggers, local tests run. With no Apex, no tests run.
wrong: `RunLocalTests` is the default only when the deployment has Apex.
The test level is optional; a default applies.
All tests run only if you ask for `RunAllTestsInOrg`.
questions.source: Metadata API Developer Guide: Running Tests in a Deployment

questions.q: A class has 30 executable statements, 6 `System.debug()` calls and 10 comment or blank lines. Its tests run 24 of the 30 statements and none of the debug calls. What coverage does Salesforce report?
options: 67%: 24 of 36 lines, with the debug calls counted
52%: 24 of all 46 lines in the class file
75%: debug calls count as covered lines by default
80%: 24 of the 30 executable statements
questions.explain: Coverage counts only executable lines. Comments, blank lines and `System.debug()` calls are left out. So it's 24 of 30, which is 80%.
wrong: `System.debug()` calls aren't counted in coverage.
Comments and blank lines aren't counted either.
Debug calls are left out, not counted as covered.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Code Coverage Best Practices
